skills.trigger: When evaluating a well-circumscribed, rounded mediastinal opacity on a lateral chest X-ray to determine its specific etiology based on location and mass effect.
steps: Assess the margins of the opacity; identify if it is well-circumscribed and rounded (suggesting a cyst or benign lesion) versus ill-defined or lobulated (suggesting malignancy like lymphoma).
Determine the precise anatomical compartment on the lateral view (e.g., middle mediastinum near the carina/trachea vs. anterior retrosternal space vs. posterior paraspinal region).

Evaluate the direction of tracheal displacement caused by the mass; specifically, note if a middle mediastinal mass causes anterior bowing of the trachea (characteristic of bronchogenic cysts) versus posterior displacement (characteristic of esophageal lesions) or lateral deviation.
